newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chirac meets Yeltsin, sees "historic" NATO treaty.
newsitem.headline: Chirac meets Yeltsin, sees "historic" NATO treaty.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac met President Boris Yeltsin on Sunday for an hour of talks on the NATO-Russia treaty due to be signed in Paris on May 27.

He told reporters before flying home that all difficulties between Moscow and NATO had been resolved and he expected "a historic signing" next week in the French capital of an accord which was "a great victory for Russia."

A Kremlin statement said the meeting, during a stopover on Chirac's return from a state visit to China, was held in "a spirit of openness and mutual understanding." Talks focused on the treaty signing but also touched on bilateral ties, it said.

"There will be an historic signing of the Russia-NATO accord, which will both erase Yalta and confirm peace on our continent for the future," Chirac said, referring to the Yalta agreement which divided Europe between Soviet and Western spheres of influence after World War Two.
Asked if there were any remaining problems with the treaty, announced by Russian and NATO negotiators last week, he said: "I think no ambiguity remains."

Under the deal, Moscow, which has strongly opposed NATO plans to expand into eastern Europe, will gain a say in the alliance's decisions and receive assurances that the West will not move nuclear and other weapons closer to Russia's borders.

Chirac, who has been outspoken among Western leaders in warning against offending or isolating Russia, hailed the accord as victory for Moscow, saying Yeltsin had successfully defended Russia's interests.

"It's a great success for Russia and it's a success that is due to the firm determination of President Yeltsin, who wanted Russia, naturally, to have its full role as great power in the new organisation of the peace," he said.

"A year and half, two years ago, Russia felt a bit humiliated or threatened and that was not acceptable," he said. The treaty was therefore "a great victory for Russia" and "a personal victory for President Yeltsin."
"It is an historic accord for western Europe, for America, for Russia and, I would say, for the world," he added.
